:::{#thm-newton-model}
#### The Newton step minimizes the quadratic model

Let $f$ be as in @def-newton-method, let $\vx$ be a point,
and write $\vecf{g} \eqdef \deriv{\vx} f(\vx)$ and $\matr{H} \eqdef \matr{H}_f(\vx)$,
with $\matr{H}$ [positive definite](linear-algebra.qmd#def-positive-definite).
The **quadratic model** of $f$ at $\vx$ is the function of a step $\vecf{\delta} \in \reals^p$

$$
q(\vecf{\delta}) \eqdef f(\vx) + \tp{\vecf{g}} \vecf{\delta} + \tfrac{1}{2}\,\tp{\vecf{\delta}} \matr{H} \vecf{\delta},
$$

the second-order Taylor polynomial of $f$ at $\vx$ (compare @thm-taylor-mv).
Its unique minimizer is the Newton step $\vecf{\delta}^* = -\matr{H}^{-1} \vecf{g}$.

:::

::: proof

$\matr{H}$ is invertible and symmetric,
because it is positive definite
([positive definite inverse](linear-algebra.qmd#thm-pd-inverse)),
so $\vecf{\delta}^*$ exists and $\matr{H} \vecf{\delta}^* = -\vecf{g}$.
For any $\vecf{d} \in \reals^p$, first

$$
\ba
\tp{\vecf{d}} \matr{H} \vecf{\delta}^*
&= -\tp{\vecf{d}} \vecf{g}
&& \text{(} \matr{H} \vecf{\delta}^* = -\vecf{g} \text{)}
\\
&= -\tp{\vecf{g}} \vecf{d},
&& \text{(a } 1 \times 1 \text{ matrix equals its transpose)}
\ea
$$

and $\tp{\vecf{\delta}^*} \matr{H} \vecf{d} = \tp{\vecf{d}} \matr{H} \vecf{\delta}^*$ in the same way, using $\tp{\matr{H}} = \matr{H}$. Then

$$
\ba
q(\vecf{\delta}^* + \vecf{d})
&= f(\vx) + \tp{\vecf{g}} \vecf{\delta}^* + \tp{\vecf{g}} \vecf{d}
+ \tfrac{1}{2} \paren{\tp{\vecf{\delta}^*} \matr{H} \vecf{\delta}^* + \tp{\vecf{\delta}^*} \matr{H} \vecf{d} + \tp{\vecf{d}} \matr{H} \vecf{\delta}^* + \tp{\vecf{d}} \matr{H} \vecf{d}}
&& \text{(definition of } q \text{; distribute)}
\\
&= f(\vx) + \tp{\vecf{g}} \vecf{\delta}^* + \tp{\vecf{g}} \vecf{d}
+ \tfrac{1}{2}\,\tp{\vecf{\delta}^*} \matr{H} \vecf{\delta}^* - \tp{\vecf{g}} \vecf{d} + \tfrac{1}{2}\,\tp{\vecf{d}} \matr{H} \vecf{d}
&& \text{(both cross terms equal } -\tp{\vecf{g}} \vecf{d} \text{)}
\\
&= q(\vecf{\delta}^*) + \tfrac{1}{2}\,\tp{\vecf{d}} \matr{H} \vecf{d},
&& \text{(cancel; definition of } q \text{)}
\ea
$$

which is greater than $q(\vecf{\delta}^*)$ for every $\vecf{d} \ne \vzero_{p \times 1}$, since $\matr{H}$ is positive definite.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-newton-model}
#### The model at $x = 2.5$

For $f(x) = \tfrac{1}{3} x^3 - 4x$ at $x = 2.5$ (@exm-newton-method),
$g = 2.5^2 - 4 = 2.25$ and $H = [5]$, so
$q(\delta) = f(2.5) + 2.25\,\delta + 2.5\,\delta^2$.
Its derivative $2.25 + 5 \delta$ is $0$ at $\delta^* = -0.45$, the Newton step,
and $2.5 - 0.45 = 2.05 = x^{(1)}$.

:::
